steps.title: Reds
steps.body: Cabernet Sauvignon is Stellenbosch's most important red, giving structured wines with blackcurrant, cedar, herbs and fresh acidity, often compared with Bordeaux. Merlot, Cabernet Franc, Shiraz and Pinotage also thrive. Bordeaux-style blends are a strength; estates like Kanonkop, Meerlust and Rustenberg are famous.

steps.title: Whites
steps.body: Chenin Blanc, called Steen locally, is widely planted, giving everything from fresh, fruity wines to rich, oaked old-vine wines. Sauvignon Blanc and Chardonnay thrive on cooler, higher sites. South Africa has more Chenin Blanc than any other country.

steps.prompt: Match each grape to its role.

steps.body: Look for wards on labels, like Simonsberg-Stellenbosch or Helderberg. They help you find specific sites within the region.

steps.prompt: What is Chenin Blanc's traditional South African name?

steps.title: What you learned
points: Cabernet Sauvignon and Bordeaux blends lead the reds
Chenin Blanc, or Steen, is widely planted
Sauvignon and Chardonnay thrive on cooler sites
